reviewRule: Pass the set when it has 1-2 genuinely usable/excellent options and no should-not-show option. Reserve hasHarmfulOption for should-not-show output, not ordinary weakness or serious mismatch.

items.text: Please come down and wash your hands. It's dinner time.
items.intent: Preserve the transition downstairs, handwashing, and dinner timing.

items.text: Please come down and wash your hands. It's dinner time.

review.why: "fewwerwords" should result in shorter statements. Good examples here would be something like. "Dinner's ready. We could wash hands." or "Those hands might be dirty for dinner time!"

items.text: Please come down and wash your hands. It's dinner time.
items.intent: Preserve the transition downstairs, handwashing, and dinner timing.

translations.translation: Dinner is ready on the table. Time to wash hands.
Dinner is prepared. Handwashing happens, then eating.
The table is set for dinner. Handwashing usually comes before sitting down to eat.

review.why: Option 1 is close. It matches the right tone, but "time to wash hands" is too direct for declarative language. Something like "Dinenr is ready on the table. We could wash hands." is softer and more declarative. The other options don't really work conversationally. These are all rather short and could be expanded by a few words to make room for better responses. The "fewerwords" responses are about the same length as these and are as brief as you can get, so feel free to use more words when it helps the responses.

items.text: Please come down and wash your hands. It's dinner time.

review.why: Options 1 and 2 are both fun and do a good job of becoming humorous. 3 and 4 are OK, but simply adding an exclamation point to a response doesn't really make it "humorous" or fun.

items.text: Please come down and wash your hands. It's dinner time.
items.intent: Preserve the transition downstairs, handwashing, and dinner timing.

translations.translation: The dinner aroma is starting to fill the downstairs area. Hands often enjoy a quick splash before joining the meal.

review.why: There are some good fun bits in here (hands often enjoy a quick splash, sink is open for a quick hand party, etc.) but these all read awkwardly AND are not shortened to match the "fewerwords" filter. FewerWords can often make phrases choppy and that's fine, but that means we should really be cutting out filler words. Consider option 1. A better "fewerwords" option might be "Smells like dinner. We can splash hands a bit and eat."

items.text: Please come down and wash your hands. It's dinner time.

items.text: Please come down and wash your hands. It's dinner time.
items.intent: Preserve coming down, handwashing, and dinner timing.

translations.translation: Dinner is ready downstairs, and the sink is the stop before eating.
The table is set; clean hands come before dinner.
Food is ready downstairs after a quick handwash.
The dinner path has two parts: downstairs and hands first.

review.why: I like option3. Even though it is brief and to the point, it actually is a nice version of declarative language. The others seem too short and don't have a conversational nature to them. That terseness takes away from some of the declarative nature of the responses.

items.text: Please come down and wash your hands. It's dinner time.
items.intent: Preserve coming down, handwashing, and dinner timing.

translations.translation: Dinner is ready.
The table is waiting.
Hands are a thing.
Food is downstairs.

review.why: Even with the FewerWords filter, we need to reflect the full scope of what the input is getting at. This person is trying to communicate that the child needs to wash hands and eat dinner now. Responses like "food is downstairs" is generally OK from a declarative standpoint, but doesn't mention washing hands, which is important. "Hands are a thing" is bizarre and not even close to helpful. An example that might work with fewerwords ON is "We could wash hands for dinner." It's a softer approach (we could) and mentions both washing hands and dinner without become a demand.

items.text: Please come down and wash your hands. It's dinner time.
items.intent: Preserve dinner sequence while using Pokemon only if natural.
